subject: Biotechnology
title: What Is a Biopharmaceutical
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Is a Biopharmaceutical usable.

hook.text: Aspirin is made by chemistry — insulin is made by living cells. That difference defines biopharmaceuticals.

buildup.text: Traditional drugs are small molecules synthesized chemically — biologics are large proteins grown in cells.

discovery.text: Biologics include antibodies, hormones, enzymes, and vaccines — they target disease with molecular precision.

twist.text: Biologics cannot be taken as pills — their protein structures would be destroyed by stomach acid.

climax.text: Biopharmaceuticals now account for over 40% of drug revenue — and the share keeps growing every year.

punchline.text: Living cells make the medicine — biology beats chemistry for complex diseases.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between biopharmaceuticals and traditional drugs?
options: Biopharmaceuticals are always cheaper to produce
Biopharmaceuticals are large proteins produced by living cells, not chemical synthesis
Traditional drugs cannot treat chronic diseases

details.summary: A biopharmaceutical is a therapeutic product derived from biological sources using biotechnology, including proteins, antibodies, nucleic acids, and living cells. Unlike chemical drugs synthesized from simple reactions, biologics are produced by living systems and have complex molecular structures.
details.whyItMatters: Biopharmaceuticals represent over 40 percent of new drug approvals and the fastest-growing segment of the pharmaceutical industry.
takeaways: Biologics are complex molecules produced by living cells rather than chemistry
They include antibodies, proteins, vaccines, and cell and gene therapies
Biopharmaceuticals account for over 40 percent of new drug approvals

faq.question: What makes a biopharmaceutical different from a regular drug?
faq.answer: Traditional drugs are small molecules made by chemical synthesis with exact, reproducible structures. Biopharmaceuticals are large complex molecules like proteins produced by living cells. They require refrigeration, injection rather than oral dosing, and cannot be exactly replicated by competitors.

faq.question: What are the most commercially successful biopharmaceutical products?
faq.answer: Humira, an anti-TNF antibody for autoimmune diseases, became the best-selling drug in history at over 20 billion dollars annually. Keytruda for cancer, Eylea for eye disease, and Stelara for inflammation are other top sellers. Seven of the top ten drugs by revenue are biologics.
